## Regime Metadata

Which rule-set, which edition, which clause: `regime` ("ISO 9001:2015"), `version`, `clause` ("§8.4.2"), `clauseTitle`, a link to the Certification Authority that owns it, and a `url` to the clause text. `reference` is derived ("ISO 9001:2015 §8.4.2"). A control means nothing without the clause it satisfies, and auditors speak in clause numbers.

```ts
import { RegimeMetadataField } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/audit/regime-metadata-field';
@field regime = contains(RegimeMetadataField);
```

Domain-neutral on purpose — this row comes from the BSL v0 design records, where a regime is a Boxel standard and a clause is one of its sections. "ISO 9001:2015 §8.5.1" and "Card Conventions §3.2" are the same shape; nothing here names a compliance-only concept. A regime-level reference leaves `clause` empty.

## Example
The contained example is ISO 9001:2015 §8.4.2 (type and extent of control of externally provided processes). The authority link is left unset in the example; Certification Authority is its own card with its own Spec.

## Non-goals
Does not carry the clause text (licensed content — `url` points at it). Not the rule: a Validation Rule contains a Regime Metadata and adds the testable statement. Not the certificate.
